description: Wake County, North Carolina (Raleigh; FIPS 37183) commercial, industrial and apartment parcels from the NC OneMap statewide parcel layer (Wake County Assessor attributes). See docs/registry/data-policy.md and the review record in docs/registry/sources/nc-wake-parcels.md.

sources.publisher: NC OneMap (NC Center for Geographic Information and Analysis), from the Wake County Assessor
sources.license: NC OneMap free and unrestricted use policy (Terms page: partner organizations share content 'at no charge' under 'this free and unrestricted use policy'; 'Written release agreements to authorize use of the geospatial data ... are not required and will not be issued'; 'Any sale of this data must not violate applicable state laws or regulations'). The dataset item's licenseInfo points to that page. Underlying records are public records under N.C. Gen. Stat. ch. 132
sources.ai_use: Not addressed by the publisher; no restriction found (the Terms page and the dataset item are silent on AI use)
sources.redistribution: Permitted (free and unrestricted use; no release agreement). Citation requested: NC OneMap, NC Department of Information Technology, Government Data Analytics Center, Center for Geographic Information and Analysis; source counties are the data stewards
sources.notes: Statewide layer 'North Carolina Parcels (Polygons)' (item 1de3d7d828ce4813b838ddf055b40317, FeatureServer layer 1, 5,938,804 parcels for 100 counties on 2026-11-03; Wake = 435,380). The Hub download API builds a CSV for a filtered request (HTTP 202 'Pending' on the first call, 200 with the file on a repeat); the URL here filters to Wake (cntyfips 183) and the Wake land classes COM (commercial), IND (industrial) and APT (apartment), about 10,000 rows, instead of the 2-GB statewide file. parusecode is county-specific: Wake's three-letter codes are NC OneMap's names for the Wake County land class letters C, D, G (see the review record); other counties need their own mapping. The full Wake file (all 435,380 parcels, about 220 MB as CSV) would run from GitHub's network. Wake County's own extract (services.wake.gov/realdata_extracts/, 42 MB zip, linked from wake.gov) is not used: services.wake.gov/robots.txt is 'User-agent: *' 'Disallow: /'. robots.txt: www.nconemap.gov and hub.arcgis.com set Crawl-delay 60 and disallow only /sites/, /admin/, /sessions/, /groups/, /people/, /workspace/; services.nconemap.gov has none (404).
